title: 第13章 西边捡来的项西(13)

content_zh:
像他们这样的出去跟人说自己是干吗的，都得现编瞎话。
几个人在屋里窝了一下午，包饺子，那女的还做了几个菜，手艺凑合，像是在饭店拿过来的剩菜的水平。
夜里他们张罗着放鞭炮的时候，项西穿上外套出了门，在大街上漫无目的地转悠着。
四周开始不断响起鞭炮声时，他在一个垃圾筒边上看到了一只狗，蜷缩着，看来是第一次经历过年，被这些响声吓坏了。
项西本来还想着，自己的那条狗，过年的时候就拿个纸箱给它装上放在后院的，结果也没机会了。
他摸了摸口袋里的一块糖，往垃圾筒旁边走了两步，又停下了。
最后他跟狗面对面地蹲着听了一会儿鞭炮声还是转身走了，他怕这狗再跟着他。
他现在保护不了任何东西，连条狗都保不住，事实已经证明了。
奶奶家客厅里摆了两桌，一桌大人，一张小桌坐着孩子，今年过年人特别齐，他们一家，二叔老叔加上两个姑，几家人从老到小都齐了。
程博衍坐在奶奶身边，屋里热闹的说笑声和孩子的尖叫声充斥着，两个婶婶隔着桌子跟老妈喊着话聊天，奶奶跟他说话他都得把耳朵凑过去才听得清。
“你爸给你压岁钱了没？”奶奶问他。
程博衍笑了：“我都多大了还给啊？没给。”
“我给他压岁钱一直给到你出生呢！”奶奶转头看着坐在另一边的老爸：“你怎么这么抠？”
“我怎么就抠了？”老爸被说愣了。
“压岁钱呢？”奶奶伸出手。
“你的？我一进门不就给你了吗？”老爸说。
“博衍的！”奶奶推了他一下。
“奶奶，”程博衍靠在椅背上笑了半天，“别折腾我爸了，他昨天还上手术台了，这会儿没回过神来呢，你再把他折腾迷糊了。”
“真是，”奶奶啧啧啧几声，“这么老了，也不怕身体吃不消。”
“我还不算太老，”老爸笑笑，拿着筷子的手举到奶奶眼前，“还稳着呢。”

“看不见，我老了。”奶奶拍开他的手。
“过完年把白内障手术做了吧，”老妈在一边说了一句，“别拖了，小手术没事的。”
“不做，万一下不来了呢，”奶奶一听就站了起来，走到小孩那桌一坐，“祖奶跟你们聊会儿。”
“明天值班？”老爸转过头看着程博衍。
“初二，”程博衍说，“不过明天我也打算过去看看，这几天怕忙不过来。”
“这两天……我和你妈要去……”老爸有些犹豫地说，“今年你去吗？”
“不去了，”程博衍没看老爸，夹了口菜放到碗里，“我不去了。”
“你别管他。”老妈推了老爸一把，把自己的杯子递到程博衍面前：“儿子，给我来点儿红酒。”
“我也来点儿。”二婶也伸过了杯子，“哎，嫂子，你这次拿的红酒真是不错！”
“你要喜欢我再给你拿两瓶，”老妈笑着说，“这个平时可以喝一点儿的。”
程博衍给她们倒好酒，奶奶喊着厨房还有菜，他放下酒瓶：“我去拿。”
刚想站起来，感觉裤腰被拽住了，条件反射就觉得是程炫宇那个烦人的土堆，他回手一抓，却抓到一只软绵绵的小手。
“哎？小溪？”他回过头，发现两岁的小外甥女不知道什么时候站在了他身后，拉着他的皮带，他刮了刮她的鼻子，“舅舅带你去厨房偷吃的好不好？”
小溪点点头，程博衍蹲下把她用胳膊一夹，往厨房走去。
“妈呀，”表姐看着他喊了一声，“博衍，你这抱孩子的技能都多少年了也没点儿提高，还能不能行了啊！”
“你闺女野着呢，”程博衍笑着说，低头问小溪，“好玩吗？”
小姑娘没说话，只是甩着胳膊一通咯咯地乐。
厨房的锅里还蒸着两大碗梅菜扣肉，程博衍一看就想笑，这是奶奶的最爱，桌上还放着两大碗芋头扣肉，这儿居然还蒸着两碗。
他用刀切了一小块肉让小溪捏着慢慢吃，拿了个盘子把扣肉给装了出来。
“哥哥，”小溪扯了扯他的裤子，“还要。”

“……叫舅舅，怎么老叫哥啊，”程博衍又切了一小条肉让她拿着，“吃吧，吃完了再出去，一会儿让你妈看见要说我了。”
小溪低头咬了一口，又把手往他嘴边一伸：“哥哥吃。”

content_en:
When people like them go out and tell people what they do, they have to make up lies.
A few people stayed in the room all afternoon, making dumplings. The woman also cooked a few dishes, and her skills were just right, as if they were leftovers from a restaurant.
When they were setting off firecrackers at night, Xiang west put on his coat and went out, wandering aimlessly on the street.
When the sound of firecrackers started to sound all around, he saw a dog curled up next to a garbage can. It seemed that it was experiencing the New Year for the first time and was frightened by the noise.
Xiang west originally thought that he would put his dog in a cardboard box and put it in the backyard during the Chinese New Year, but he didn't have a chance.
He touched a piece of candy in his pocket, took two steps toward the trash can, and then stopped.
In the end, he squatted face to face with the dog and listened to the sound of firecrackers for a while before turning around and walking away. He was afraid that the dog would follow him again.
He couldn't protect anything now, not even a dog, and it had been proven.
There are two tables in the living room of grandma's house, one for adults and one for children. This year's New Year's Eve is especially crowded. Their family, including the second uncle and two aunts, has all the family members from old to young.
Cheng Boyan sat next to his grandma, and the room was filled with lively laughter and children's screams. The two aunts were shouting and chatting with his mother across the table. He had to put his ears close to hear what his grandma was talking to him.
"Did your dad give you any New Year's money?" Grandma asked him.
Cheng Boyan smiled: "How old am I to give it back? No."
"I gave him New Year's money until you were born!" Grandma turned to look at Dad sitting on the other side: "Why are you so stingy?"
"Why did I pick it?" Dad was stunned when he was told.
"Where's the new year's money?" Grandma stretched out her hand.
"Yours? Didn't I give it to you as soon as I walked in the door?" Dad said.
"Bo Yan's!" Grandma pushed him.
"Grandma," Cheng Boyan leaned back in the chair and smiled for a long time, "Don't torment my dad. He was on the operating table yesterday and he hasn't come back to his senses now. You torment him again and make him confused."
"Really," grandma clicked her tongue, "I'm so old, and I'm not afraid that my body won't be able to handle it."
"I'm not too old yet," Dad smiled and raised the hand holding the chopsticks in front of Grandma's eyes, "I'm still stable."
"You can't see, I'm old." Grandma slapped his hand away.
"Let's have cataract surgery after the Chinese New Year," my mother said on the side, "Don't delay, the minor surgery will be fine."
"No, in case you don't come," grandma stood up and walked to the children's table to sit down. "Grandma will chat with you for a while."
"On duty tomorrow?" Dad turned his head and looked at Cheng Boyan.
"It's the second day of junior high school," Cheng Boyan said, "but I plan to go over there tomorrow and have a look. I'm afraid I won't be able to do it these days."
"In the next two days...your mother and I are going..." Dad said hesitantly, "Are you going this year?"
"I'm not going," Cheng Boyan didn't look at his father, picked up some food and put it in a bowl, "I'm not going."
"Don't worry about him." Mom pushed dad and handed her cup to Cheng Boyan: "Son, give me some red wine."
"I'll have some too." The second aunt also stretched out her cup, "Hey, sister-in-law, the red wine you got this time is really good!"
"If you like it, I'll get you two more bottles," my mother said with a smile, "You can usually drink a little of this."
Cheng Boyan poured wine for them. Grandma shouted that there were still dishes in the kitchen. He put down the wine bottle and said, "I'll get it."
Just as he was about to stand up, he felt the waistband of his pants being pulled. His conditioned reflex thought it was Cheng Xuanyu's annoying mound. He reached back and grabbed it, only to find a limp little hand.
"Huh? Xiaoxi?" He turned around and found that his two-year-old niece was standing behind him at some point, pulling on his belt. He scratched her nose, "Can uncle take you to the kitchen to eat secretly?"
Xiaoxi nodded, Cheng BoYan knelt down and hugged her with his arm, and walked to the kitchen.
"Oh my god," my cousin looked at him and shouted, "Bo Yan, your child-holding skills haven't improved at all over the years, can you still do it?"
"Your daughter is wild," Cheng Boyan said with a smile, lowered his head and asked Xiaoxi, "Is it fun?"
The little girl didn't say anything, she just waved her arms and giggled.
There were two large bowls of braised pork with pickles and pickles steaming in the kitchen pot. Cheng Boyan wanted to laugh when he saw it. This was grandma's favorite. There were also two large bowls of braised pork with taro on the table. There were actually two bowls steaming here.
He cut a small piece of meat with a knife and let Xiao Xi eat it slowly. He took a plate and put the meat on it.
"Brother," Xiaoxi tugged at his pants, "I want more."
"...Call me uncle, why do you always call me brother?" Cheng Boyan cut another small piece of meat for her to hold, "Eat it, then go out after eating, your mother will tell you about me later if she sees it."
Xiaoxi lowered his head and took a bite, then stretched his hand to his mouth: "Brother, eat it."
